lines_of_business: Health benefit plans administered by Cigna Companies; benefit plan document supersedes
Medicare section lists NCD/LCDs for reference only
sections_in_order: Coverage Policy (Ambulatory External; Mobile Cardiac Monitoring with Telemetry; Ambulatory Implantable - ADULT; Implantable - PEDIATRIC; Cardiac Self-Monitoring)
criteria_location: Coverage Policy, pp.2-4 (about 2.5 pages). Coding Information pp.4-18 (heavy ICD-10 tables). General Background pp.18-28 evidence. Revision Details p.34.
procedures_covered: Ambulatory external cardiac monitoring 48 h to 30 days (93241-93248, 93268, 93270-93272, 0937T-0940T)
Implantable loop recorder adult (33285, C1764) and pediatric <=21

logic.top_level: pathways (one block per device; adult vs pediatric ILR), each any-of; some indications carry nested all-of

k_of_n.quote: considered medically necessary when ANY of the following criteria are met

logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: Closing 'any other indication' not covered statement per device; pediatric ILR has an explicit 'not medically necessary' list (reflex syncope with frequent/severe episodes, epilepsy, etc.); self-monitoring devices excluded as convenience items.
logic.initial_vs_repeat: ILR replacement allowed if 'continues to meet ALL of the above criteria and the existing monitor is no longer under warranty and cannot be repaired'. No repeat-study interval for external monitors.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: following stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA) of undetermined cause (CPT 93268, 93270-93272)
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: The CPT list in parentheses restricts this one bullet to event-monitor codes, so an item-level code condition is embedded in a clinical bullet

and_or_ambiguity.quote: continues to meet ALL of the above criteria
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: The ILR list is ANY-of; 'ALL of the above' can't be literal (patient could not satisfy both syncope and CTI ablation bullets)

and_or_ambiguity.quote: if an individual is identified with atrial fibrillation in the setting of acute medical illness or surgery, especially in those who underwent noncardiac surgery and with risk factors for stroke (e.g., CHA2DS2-VASc* score >=2)
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: 'especially' and 'e.g.' make the CHA2DS2-VASc threshold look optional

requirement_kinds.quote: symptoms of presyncope, syncope, or severe palpitations when there is clinical suspicion of a significant bradyarrhythmia or tachyarrhythmia

definitions_that_change_meaning.definition_quote: CHA2DS2-VASc is a clinical risk score for prediction of stroke and systemic embolism: Congestive heart failure or left ventricular dysfunction, hypertension, age >=75 (doubled), diabetes, stroke (doubled)-vascular disease, age 65-74, sex category.

extraction_hazards: Coding Information is ~14 pages of repeated ICD-10 tables with repeated headers ('Medical Coverage Policy: 0547')
Footnote asterisk defines CHA2DS2-VASc, split from the bullet it modifies
Rows labeled 'Not Covered or Reimbursable' sit among covered tables
Adult vs pediatric ILR sections look alike
General Background (~10 pages) and references (~6 pages) after the criteria
Cigna ILR bullets repeat the same text as the external/MCOT bullets (copied bullets)
interesting_structures: Same 5-7 indication bullets reused across external, MCOT and ILR (copy-paste family)
MCOT is escalation: needs non-diagnostic external monitoring AND an indication
CHA2DS2-VASc risk score as a threshold
Adult vs pediatric split by age <=21
Revision history shows which statements changed and when

fit_to_tree.why: Mostly any-of lists with a few all-of children and numeric thresholds; ICD tables help. Hazards are copy-pasted bullets, 'e.g.' thresholds and forward-looking intent.
